clue.text: Article about another title for Macbeth

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first article encloses the second

parts.note: THE is the definite article
another article, the indefinite AN

explanation.surface: A grammar point about Macbeth being given a second title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is read as another article, not another title; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is Thane of Glamis and then of Cawdor, a Scottish noble rank.

clue.text: One 'cut Marat in' pieces shocking!

indicators.note: in pieces means broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Marat stabbed in his bath, a horrifying scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pieces' rearranges I (one) with CUT MARAT; Marat was murdered in his bath in 1793.
explanation.definitionFit: Something traumatic is deeply distressing, causing shock.

clue.text: What an actor seeks on one side

explanation.surface: An actor auditioning, standing to the side.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor looks for a role in a play, and set aside or to one side is the second sense.

clue.text: See Miss St Clare work up speed and disappear from view

parts.note: Eva St Clare is little Eva in Uncle Tom's Cabin

indicators.note: up in a down clue means this word is read bottom to top

parts.note: OP, opus, is a work
rate means speed

explanation.surface: Watching a young lady put on speed and vanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns OP into PO; 'See' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaporate is to vanish, as a liquid becomes vapour.

clue.text: Attractive as a very quiet part of London

parts.note: PP, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet
Ealing is a district of west London

explanation.surface: Praising a hushed corner of London as charming.
explanation.walkthrough: EALING is a borough in west London; 'as' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something appealing draws you in, a synonym of attractive.

clue.text: Goddess not quite a beginner

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a starter is one who begins

explanation.surface: A novice who is almost divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims the last letter from STARTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Astarte was the Phoenician goddess of fertility and love.

clue.text: Studied second-hand material put up at first

indicators.note: at first places that piece before the other
put up in a down clue means this word is turned to read upwards

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
used means second-hand

explanation.surface: Examining old cloth hung up beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' signals the reversal, natural in a down clue; 'at first' places the fabric before the second-hand piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse something is to read it carefully, to examine it.

clue.text: Jack holds up gang with a deadly weapon

indicators.note: holds means the sailor's letters wrap round the next piece

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a jack or sailor

indicators.note: up in a down clue reverses the word for the gang

parts.note: a mob is a gang

explanation.surface: A sailor robbing a gang at gunpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is a sailor here, not a card or a robber; 'up' reverses the gang and 'holds' wraps it; 'with a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The atomic bomb is the most destructive weapon of war.

clue.text: Little bird's proverbial role

parts.note: from the saying 'a little bird told me', said when hiding who passed on a secret

explanation.surface: The part a small bird plays in a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial little bird is the unnamed source who tells secrets, a tell-tale.

clue.text: Fool, an unknown quantity here on the cricket field

parts.note: to gull is to fool, and a gull is a dupe
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A dupe of a cricketer standing somewhere obscure in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Gully is a cricket fielding position near the slips.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a fielding position near the slips takes this name.

clue.text: Sculptor's material fashioned as a table? Right

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made anew, so the letters of these words are reworked

explanation.surface: Asking whether a piece of furniture was carved from a sculptor's stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' rearranges AS A TABLE into ALABASTE; R finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a soft white stone long carved by sculptors.

clue.text: Refuse what butchers sell

explanation.surface: A shopper turning down the butcher's wares.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal means waste or rubbish, and also the edible organs such as liver and kidney sold at a butcher's.

clue.text: Maxim of many an .emperor

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors

explanation.surface: A saying attributed to plenty of rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: M for 'many' is a crossword convention from the Roman numeral 1000; Otto I was a German emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto is a short guiding saying, a synonym of maxim.

clue.text: Rude expression for a kind of tart

explanation.surface: Blowing a rude noise at a fruit pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A raspberry is a jeering noise made with the tongue and lips, and also a soft red fruit used in tarts.

clue.text: A way to test the 'solution might cause-a titter

indicators.note: might cause suggests the following letters can be turned into something new

explanation.surface: A chemistry practical where the lab work makes pupils giggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might cause' signals that A TITTER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To titrate is to measure a chemical solution's concentration by adding a reagent drop by drop.

clue.text: Another word for Captain Horatio's second instrument

definitions.text: Another word for Captain Horatio's second instrument

parts.words: Another word for Captain Horatio's second instrument
parts.note: Captain Horatio Hornblower's surname splits as horn plus blower, and blower is British slang for a phone

explanation.surface: Musing on a naval captain's second musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Horatio Hornblower is C S Forester's naval hero; 'blower' is British slang for a phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Blower is British slang for a phone, the instrument used to call someone.

clue.text: Puncture adjoining white notes by inserting a black one

indicators.note: by inserting means a further piece is set inside the first one

parts.note: D and E are neighbouring white keys on a piano
E flat is the black key lying between D and E

explanation.surface: A music lesson about piano keys, white ones with a black one between.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by inserting' puts E FLAT, the black key between D and E, inside DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflate a tyre is to let the air out, as a puncture does.

clue.text: Infantry. race in support of railwaymen

parts.note: foot soldiers are infantry
a plate is a horse race for a prize

explanation.surface: Soldiers racing to back the rail workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The footplate is the platform where a steam train's driver and fireman stand.

clue.text: Connie, put out, swallows anger to make peace proposal

indicators.note: swallows means the rearranged name takes in the next piece
put out means upset, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Connie, upset, holds her temper to offer a truce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' signals the anagram of the name, and 'swallows' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An eirenicon is a proposal offered to bring about peace.

clue.text: Prayer in order for sidesmen during the offertory

explanation.surface: Church business: the order of service and the ushers passing plates round.
explanation.definitionFit: A collect is a short prayer set in the order of service, and to gather money is what sidesmen do with the plates at the offertory.

clue.text: Tin fish — from Bangalore?

explanation.surface: Canned fish shipped from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin fish is naval slang for an underwater missile, and the Bangalore is a tube explosive used to clear wire.

clue.text: There's nothing 'in the duty list for Chanticleer

indicators.note: in means the first piece is placed inside the duty list

parts.note: a roster is a rota of duties
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A rota left blank for the farmyard bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Chanticleer is the cockerel in Chaucer and in fables.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanticleer is the traditional name of the cock in folk tales, a male farmyard bird.

clue.text: Restaurant's starter is fish or meat ball

indicators.note: starter means the first letter of the word

parts.note: sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A restaurant's first course offering a choice of fish or meatball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a fried ball of minced meat.

clue.text: Drink needed when pachyderm damaged cars

parts.note: a hippo is a thick-skinned beast, a pachyderm

indicators.note: damaged means knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Needing a stiff drink after a hippo wrecked the cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges CARS into CRAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocras is an old spiced wine drunk in medieval times.

clue.text: Egyptian god's burden, being beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means losing the top, here the first letter

parts.note: the burden of a song is its refrain, its chorus

explanation.surface: The load an Egyptian deity bears before being beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' removes the first letter of CHORUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Horus is the falcon-headed sky deity of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Fat return, seen among these boys

indicators.note: return means the run is read backwards
among means the letters lie within these words

explanation.surface: Overweight boys going back for seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' takes ESEBO from these boys; 'return' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very overweight.

clue.text: "I'd rather be A — suckled in a creed outworn" (Wordsworth)

definitions.text: "I'd rather be A — suckled in a creed outworn" (Wordsworth)

parts.words: "I'd rather be A — suckled in a creed outworn" (Wordsworth)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Wordsworth's sonnet The World Is Too Much With Us, the missing word being a follower of an old non-Christian faith

explanation.surface: A quotation from a Wordsworth sonnet with one word left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth wished to be a heathen raised in old nature worship rather than a jaded modern.

clue.text: What one admits, having stolen a young sow, say?

parts.note: a gilt is a young female pig

explanation.surface: A thief confessing to taking a piglet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' shows GILT, a young sow, is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who owns up admits responsibility for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Right hand' one in the French. Department

taken as written

explanation.surface: A right-hand man working in a French government department.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhône is both a river and a French département; 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône is one of the numbered administrative regions of France, named after the river.

clue.text: Being mad about himself he might perhaps come again

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A conceited man threatening to return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges COME AGAIN; 'might' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An egomaniac is a person obsessed with his own importance, wholly self-absorbed.

clue.text: Way the first woman artist made a dock labourer appear

Gustave Doré was a French illustrator

explanation.surface: Eve and an artist conjuring a docker into view.
explanation.walkthrough: Doré is the 19th-century French engraver; 'made a ... appear' is link.

clue.text: Point by which a number get taken in

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A tip on how a figure gets swallowed up.
